old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a pool table, focusing on two billiard balls. One ball, marked with the number 15, is positioned near the edge of the table, while the other, white with a red dot, is slightly behind it. A player, dressed in a red shirt, is seen in the background, holding a cue stick poised to strike. As the video progresses, the cue ball makes contact with the 15-ball, sending both rolling across the blue felt surface. The camera remains stationary throughout, maintaining a consistent angle that highlights the dynamic movement of the balls and the player's focused stance. The scene is set indoors, with a blurred background suggesting a casual or recreational environment.

caption: The video captures a close view of a blue-felt pool table where a player in a red shirt holds a wooden cue at the far rail. The cue tip contacts the red-dotted white cue ball, then draws back while the ball rolls forward. The white ball closes on the red-and-white striped 15-ball and strikes it, after which the striped ball stays near the left while the cue ball continues to its right. The balls appear larger in frame as their surfaces rotate and the motion eases. The cue moves out of view, and the blurred orange ball at the lower foreground leaves the edge. The 15-ball remains at rest on the left, while the cue ball still rolls slowly to the right.

draft_caption: The video captures a close view of a blue-felt pool table where a player in a red shirt holds a wooden cue at the far rail. The cue tip presses against a red-dotted white cue ball, then pushes it forward as the stick pulls back. The cue ball rolls toward the camera, closing on a red-and-white striped 15-ball and striking it partway through the clip. Both balls travel forward and grow larger in frame, the striped ball leading while the white ball trails and drifts to its right, surfaces rotating as the motion eases. The player's torso and cue recede out of the top of the frame, while a blurred orange ball in the lower foreground drops from view. The two balls slow to a near stop, the 15-ball on the left and the cue ball on the right.
